A company posts signs at its entrances warning that the premises are under 24-hour video surveillance. Which control type do the signs primarily represent?
Signs discourage an attacker before an attempt is made, which makes them deterrent. The cameras themselves would be detective.
Which of the following provides non-repudiation for an email message?
Encrypting the message with a symmetric key
A digital signature is made with the sender's private key, which only the sender holds, so the sender cannot plausibly deny sending it.
In a Zero Trust architecture, which component makes the decision to grant, deny or revoke access to a resource?
The policy engine (control plane) makes the decision. The policy administrator acts on it, and the policy enforcement point (data plane) enforces it.
A security analyst plants a fake administrator credential in a database. Any use of that credential triggers an alert. What is this called?
A honeytoken is a piece of fake data, such as a credential or record, that has no legitimate use, so any use of it indicates compromise.
Before applying a major patch, a change advisory board requires a documented way to return the system to its previous state if the patch fails. What is this document?
A backout plan (rollback plan) describes how to reverse a change if it causes problems.
A company compares its current security controls against the NIST Cybersecurity Framework to identify which controls are missing. What is this activity?
A gap analysis compares the current state with a target framework or baseline to find missing controls.
A user downloads an ISO image and wants to verify that it was not altered. Which should be used?
Comparing a SHA-256 hash with the published value verifies integrity. AES is encryption, RSA is asymmetric crypto, and ECDHE is key exchange.
Which technique makes stored password hashes more resistant to brute-force attacks by deliberately increasing the computation time per guess?
Key stretching algorithms (PBKDF2, bcrypt, Argon2) run many iterations, which slows each guess.
A browser needs to check, in real time, whether a server's certificate has been revoked. Which protocol is used?
OCSP returns the status of a single certificate in real time. A CRL is a downloaded list that is updated periodically.
Alice wants to send Bob a message that only Bob can read. Which key should Alice use to encrypt it?
Encrypting with the recipient's public key means only the recipient's private key can decrypt it.
What is the primary purpose of an access control vestibule?
A vestibule (mantrap) lets only one door open at a time, which stops unauthorized people following an authorized person in.
An employee receives a text message claiming to be from the bank, with a link to verify an account. Which attack is this?
Smishing is phishing over SMS. Vishing uses voice calls, and whaling targets executives.
An attacker registers 'paypa1.com' to capture credentials from users who mistype the real domain. Which attack is this?
Typosquatting relies on look-alike or misspelled domains.
Attackers compromise an industry forum that employees of a target company visit often, and use it to deliver malware to them. Which attack is this?
A watering hole attack compromises a site the target group already trusts and visits.
Which threat actor is MOST likely to have significant funding and to run long-term, persistent intrusions for espionage?
Nation-state actors are well funded and conduct advanced persistent threat (APT) campaigns.
A group defaces a government website to protest a new law. Which threat actor is MOST likely responsible?
Hacktivists are motivated by political or philosophical beliefs.
A department starts storing customer files in a personal cloud storage service that IT has not approved. What does this describe?
Shadow IT is the use of technology without the organization's approval or oversight.
A web server log shows the input ' OR 1=1 -- in a login field. Which attack is being attempted?
' OR 1=1 -- makes the WHERE clause always true and comments out the rest of the query, which is classic SQL injection.
A request to a web server contains ../../../../etc/passwd. Which attack is this?
The ../ sequences try to move outside the web root to read arbitrary files.
A user posts a comment containing a <script> tag on a forum. The script runs in the browser of every user who views the comment. Which attack is this?
The script is saved on the server and served to other users, which makes it stored (persistent) XSS.
A packet capture shows a long run of 0x90 bytes followed by shellcode sent to a service. Which attack does this indicate?
0x90 is the x86 NOP instruction. A NOP sled followed by shellcode is a typical buffer overflow exploit.
An application checks a file's permissions and then opens the file. An attacker swaps the file between those two steps. What is this vulnerability?
A TOCTOU race condition happens when the state changes between the check and the use.
Users report that their files now have a .locked extension and that a text file demands payment in cryptocurrency. What is the MOST likely cause?
Encrypted, renamed files and a ransom note are the main indicators of ransomware.
A developer plants code that deletes payroll records if their name is ever removed from the HR system. What is this?
A logic bomb runs its malicious action when a specific condition is met.
Authentication logs show a few common passwords tried once each against hundreds of different accounts. Which attack is this?
Password spraying tries a small number of common passwords across many accounts to stay under lockout thresholds.
An attacker extracts an NTLM hash from memory and uses it to authenticate to another server without cracking it. Which attack is this?
Pass-the-hash reuses the hash itself as the authenticator.
An on-path attacker forces a client and server to negotiate TLS 1.0 instead of TLS 1.3. Which attack is this?
A downgrade attack forces the use of an older, weaker protocol or cipher.
An analyst sees that several IP addresses in a host's ARP cache map to the same MAC address. Which attack is MOST likely?
ARP poisoning maps the attacker's MAC to other IPs, often the gateway, so the attacker sits on the path of the traffic.
Attackers send small DNS queries with a spoofed source address, and open resolvers send large responses to the victim. Which attack is this?
Reflected amplification uses small requests that produce much larger responses aimed at a spoofed victim.
Which action BEST reduces the attack surface of a newly deployed server?
Hardening removes anything not needed, which leaves fewer services and ports to attack.
Which mitigation BEST prevents compromised IoT devices from reaching finance servers?
Segmentation (VLANs or ACLs) isolates the IoT devices so a compromise cannot spread to sensitive systems.
What is the primary security benefit of infrastructure as code (IaC)?
It removes the need for patching
It produces consistent, repeatable configurations that can be reviewed and version-controlled
It removes the need for access control
It guarantees all data is encrypted
IaC defines environments in code, which reduces configuration drift and lets changes be reviewed like any other code.
In an IaaS cloud model, who is responsible for patching the guest operating system?
In IaaS the provider secures the physical hosts and hypervisor, and the customer manages the OS and everything above it.
A plant's operational technology network has no physical or wireless connection to any other network. What is this design called?
An air gap isolates a network physically from all others.
Administrators must first connect to a hardened intermediate host before they can manage servers in a secure zone. What is this host called?
A jump server (jump box) is a single, controlled and monitored entry point for administrative access.
Which device is BEST suited to protecting a public web application from SQL injection and XSS?
A WAF inspects HTTP traffic at Layer 7 and can block application attacks such as SQLi and XSS.
Policy requires a perimeter firewall to block all traffic if the device fails. Which behavior is required?
Fail-closed (fail-secure) blocks traffic on failure, which favors confidentiality over availability.
A security device must be able to block malicious traffic in real time. How should it be deployed?
As an IDS on a network TAP
As a sensor on a SPAN port
Only an inline device can drop traffic. TAP and SPAN deployments are passive and can only alert.
Data being processed in a server's RAM is in which state?
Data in use is data being processed in memory or by the CPU.
Which concept states that data is subject to the laws of the country where it is stored?
Data sovereignty means local law applies to data based on where it physically resides.
A payment system replaces each card number with a random value. The mapping to the real number is kept in a secure vault. What is this technique?
Tokenization swaps sensitive data for a token that has no mathematical relationship to the original value.
Support staff should see only the last four digits of a customer's card number. Which technique meets this requirement?
Masking hides part of the data in a display while keeping it partly visible.
Which metric defines the maximum acceptable amount of data loss, measured in time?
The recovery point objective is how far back in time you can afford to lose data. RTO is how long you can be down.
A company needs a recovery site that is fully equipped with current data and can take over within minutes. Which site type is required?
A hot site is fully operational and kept in sync, so failover is nearly immediate.
A full backup runs on Sunday and incremental backups run Monday through Thursday. The server fails on Friday morning. What is needed to restore it?
Sunday's full backup and Thursday's incremental
Sunday's full backup and the Monday-to-Thursday incrementals
Each incremental backup holds only the changes since the previous backup, so all of them are needed in order after the full backup.
Which provides short-term power so that servers can shut down gracefully during an outage?
A UPS provides immediate battery power for minutes. A generator provides longer-term power.
Which model delivers network security services such as a secure web gateway, CASB and ZTNA from the cloud, combined with WAN capabilities?
Secure Access Service Edge (SASE) combines SD-WAN with cloud-delivered security services.
Which source provides prescriptive configuration baselines for hardening operating systems and applications?
CIS Benchmarks are consensus hardening guides. CVSS scores vulnerabilities, STIX is a threat intelligence format, and the OWASP Top 10 lists web risks.
An employee loses a company smartphone. Which tool allows IT to wipe it remotely?
Mobile device management enforces policy and can lock or wipe devices remotely.
Which WPA3 feature replaces the pre-shared key handshake and protects against offline dictionary attacks?
Simultaneous Authentication of Equals (SAE) replaces the WPA2 PSK four-way handshake and resists offline cracking.
A company wants each Wi-Fi user to authenticate with their own directory credentials. Which should be implemented?
Open network with a captive portal
Enterprise mode uses 802.1X/EAP with a RADIUS server for per-user authentication.
A security team cannot patch effectively because it does not know which systems exist. Which process should be improved FIRST?
You cannot secure or patch what you don't know about. Asset management comes first.
Hard drives that held PHI are being retired and will not be reused. Which method BEST ensures the data cannot be recovered?
Physical destruction such as shredding guarantees the data cannot be recovered. Formatting and deleting partitions leave data recoverable.
Which type of vulnerability scan gives the most accurate patch-level results with the fewest false positives?
A credentialed scan logs in and can read installed versions directly.
A scanner reports an Apache vulnerability on a server that runs only IIS. What is this finding?
The reported vulnerability does not exist on the server, so it is a false positive.
Which system provides a numerical severity score for vulnerabilities?
CVSS scores severity from 0 to 10. CVE is an identifier and CWE classifies weakness types.
A legacy system cannot be patched because the vendor no longer supports it. What is the BEST action?
Accept the risk without documenting it
Isolate the system on a segmented network with strict ACLs
When patching isn't possible, isolation is a compensating control. The risk should also be formally documented.
Which tool aggregates logs from many sources and correlates events to generate alerts?
SIEM collects, normalizes and correlates logs. SOAR automates the response.
A SOC wants to automatically isolate hosts and block IPs using predefined playbooks. Which tool should it use?
Security orchestration, automation and response (SOAR) runs automated playbooks.
Which control can block outbound emails containing 16-digit numbers that pass a Luhn check?
Data loss prevention uses pattern matching and validators such as Luhn to detect card numbers leaving the organization.
Before a laptop is allowed onto the network, a system checks that it has current antivirus and patches. What is this system?
Network access control performs posture checks before granting access.
Which tool detects suspicious process behavior on endpoints and lets an analyst isolate a host remotely?
Endpoint detection and response monitors behavior and supports response actions such as isolation.
Which DNS record tells receiving mail servers what to do with messages that fail SPF or DKIM alignment?
DMARC publishes the policy (none, quarantine or reject) and reporting addresses.
Which combination is an example of multifactor authentication?
A smart card is something you have and a PIN is something you know. The other options use two factors of the same type.
Two organizations want single sign-on that exchanges XML-based authentication assertions. Which standard should they use?
SAML uses XML assertions between an identity provider and a service provider for federated SSO.
A user wants a third-party app to access their calendar without giving the app their password. Which standard enables this?
OAuth is an authorization framework that issues scoped access tokens.
Administrators should receive elevated rights only when needed, and those rights should expire automatically. Which BEST meets this requirement?
Permanent domain admin rights for all IT staff
A single admin password reused across systems
Privileged access management with just-in-time, time-limited elevation enforces least privilege.
Access is granted based on classification labels such as Secret and Top Secret assigned to users and data. Which access control model is this?
Mandatory access control uses labels and clearances set by the system, not by data owners.
Access depends on the user's department, the time of day and whether the device is managed. Which model is this?
Attribute-based access control evaluates multiple attributes of the user, resource and environment.
An infected host has just been isolated from the network. What is the NEXT step in incident response?
The order is preparation, detection, analysis, containment, eradication, recovery, then lessons learned. Isolation is containment, so eradication comes next.
Which document records who handled a piece of evidence and when?
Chain of custody records every transfer of evidence so it remains admissible.
During forensic collection, which should be collected FIRST?
Following the order of volatility, memory is lost at power-off, so it is collected before disk.
An asset is worth $100,000, the exposure factor is 40%, and the event is expected once every two years. What is the ALE?
A company buys cyber insurance to cover breach costs. Which risk response is this?
Insurance transfers the financial impact of the risk to a third party.
A company stops offering a product feature because its security risk is too high. Which risk response is this?
Avoidance removes the activity that creates the risk.
Which document lists identified risks with their owners, ratings and treatments?
A risk register tracks each risk, its likelihood and impact, its owner and its response.
Which assessment identifies critical business functions and the impact of their disruption?
A BIA identifies critical processes and drives RTO and RPO targets.
A contract specifies 99.9% uptime and financial penalties if it is missed. What is this agreement?
A service level agreement defines measurable service levels and the penalties for missing them.
Under an existing master agreement, which document defines the specific deliverables and timeline for a project?
A statement of work describes the specific work, deliverables and schedule under an MSA.
Which contract clause lets an organization assess a vendor's security controls?
A right-to-audit clause permits the customer to audit or assess the vendor.
A payroll provider processes employee data on behalf of a company. What is the provider's role?
The company (controller) decides the purpose, and the provider (processor) processes the data on its behalf.
Which privacy right allows an individual to request deletion of their personal data?
The right to be forgotten (erasure, under GDPR) lets data subjects request deletion.
A penetration tester is given full network diagrams and source code before testing. Which type of test is this?
In a known-environment (white-box) test, the tester has full information.
Which document defines the scope, timing and permitted techniques for a penetration test?
Rules of engagement set the boundaries of the test and give authorization.
What is the BEST way to measure whether phishing awareness training is effective?
Run simulated phishing campaigns and track click and report rates
Survey whether employees enjoyed the training
Simulated phishing gives measurable behavioral metrics: how many people click and how many report.
Which document do employees sign that defines the permitted use of company IT resources?
An acceptable use policy sets the rules for using organizational systems.
A customer is reviewing a vendor's controls. Which provides the MOST independent assurance?
An independent external audit, such as SOC 2 Type II, gives the strongest assurance because the auditor is not part of the vendor.
Which term describes the amount of risk an organization is willing to accept in pursuit of its objectives?
Risk appetite is the broad level of risk the organization will accept. Risk tolerance is the acceptable deviation from it.
Which term describes the risk that remains after controls are applied?
Residual risk is the inherent risk minus the effect of controls.
A department receives approval to deviate from a security policy for 90 days, with compensating controls in place. What is this?
An exception is a documented, approved, time-limited deviation, usually with compensating controls.
